rules.sentence: The predominant histologic finding of vesiculobullous dermatoses is acantholysis, or loss of connection between cells at various levels of the epidermis, which correlates to the blisters seen clinically.
Some classic vesiculobullous disorders include pemphigus vulgaris, Hailey-Hailey disease, and eczema herpeticum.

The predominant histologic finding of the psoriasiform disorders is acanthosis, or epidermal hyperplasia, with concurrent elongation of the rete ridges, which correlates to the thickened plaques seen clinically.
The quintessential example of a psoriasiform disorder is psoriasis vulgaris, but other examples include pityriasis rubra pilaris and pityriasis rosea.
